done_when: An upgrade close syncs Forge's files without rewriting the repo's git hooks; close replaces the pull request's Done when line after an amend; a commit changing only close's test-state record counts as bookkeeping for CI reuse; story titles are read as UTF-8; an error during close's conflicted-merge handling aborts the merge and says so; command tests cover each, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Functional. A client with `.python-version` set to `3.10` can have Forge correctly installed under Python 3.11, yet this regeneration command selects the client's incompatible interpreter. `--isolated --no-project` does not disable Python-version discovery: [uv's implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/uv/0.8.22/crates/uv/src/commands/project/run.rs) reads the pin and resolves `--with` using that interpreter. Forge requires Python >=3.11 (`pyproject.toml:9`), so a generated-file conflict incorporating an upgraded Forge pin fails dependency resolution and aborts close. The previous launcher (`src/forge/repo.py:638–643`) uses `uv tool run`, which [ignores project Python pins](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/tools/#python-versions). Land also reaches this path through `close.close` (`src/forge/land.py:54`). The package-acquisition stub executes the script in its existing interpreter (`tests/test_running_commands_follow_changed_forge_pin.py:50–55`), so the passing proofs do not detect this regression.
findings.title: Select Forge's Python when regenerating under a changed pin

stop.reason: Owner wants every in-flight fix finished; narrowed to the one remaining finding: conflict regeneration must not rewrite user-owned Husky hooks

why: Real issues the coordinator skipped, still in close (audit, 2026-10-09): an upgrade close's full sync rewrites the real repo's git hooks, an amended Done-when never reaches an existing pull request body, a test-state change forces a full CI rerun instead of reusing the parent's, the story title is read in the platform encoding, and a SyntaxError during a conflicted merge leaves the merge active
